claim: Replacing every logged PhysX convex mesh (panda_link0-7, panda_hand) by the convex hull of its own vertices changes no S4 or S5 status in any of the 3,874 C1 branches (400 scene-runs; S4 714 PASS / 1 FAIL / 3,159 NOT_APPLICABLE and S5 3,863 PASS / 11 FAIL under both geometries).
The S4 minimum distance of all 715 acted branches is unchanged to the last bit: in all 4,755 logged move rows the robot part nearest the target is a finger (box shapes, untouched by the hull).

The hull changes the hand-target distance in move rows by up to 0.242 mm (median 0.077 mm of the 3,441 changed rows) and the arm-link distance by up to 0.028 mm, always toward the target; the nearest hand distance is 17.0 mm and the nearest arm-link distance 83.0 mm, far from the 0 mm S4 threshold.

Of 211,104 unique observed contact pair rows, 21 involve a mesh (hand-held cube, two scenes); all overlap in both geometries; the hull reduces the overlap by 0.016-0.139 mm; no mesh pair is near the 1 mm S5 rule. The only change to an S5 record is the reported median penetration of one branch (0.060 -> 0.049 mm).

The logged mesh surfaces lie up to 1.23 mm (panda_link5; hand 0.43 mm) inside the hull of their vertices (0.05-0.29 % of the volume missing); the effect on C1 S4/S5 is nil because these surfaces are never the nearest geometry in a decisive row.
condition_or_limit: A larger intrinsic deviation than the 0.24 mm seen in distances; other uses of the mesh distances (e.g. arm clearance audits) were not re-analysed
